paragraphs: A signal that this is worth experiencing is being willing to listen to the service request clearly first, then check the vehicle and work order identification, and raise specific questions when items are missing. Liking cars can be a starting point for exploration, but it cannot replace an interest in repeated checking and service communication.

Learn about the actual conditions in advance: standing, moving heavy objects, hand operations, noise and weather. The shop environment differs from that of roadside service; rest, shift rotation, tools and training arrangements should be checked with the specific employer and cannot be presumed from the occupational title alone.

First distinguish shop tire service from roadside service: both may involve tire work, and roadside tasks also require checking the location, on-site conditions and cooperation. Whole-vehicle fault diagnosis, diesel engine repair and tire manufacturing are work with different task scopes.

The safety experience uses the original fictional vehicle intake material S1 from this page. Only read the records, circle the missing items and write clarifying questions; do not mount or dismount wheels, lift a vehicle, inflate, repair tires or test drive. The practice only judges whether the records in the prompt can move to the next round of professional confirmation.
What kind of work preferences suit tire repairers and changers?

You can observe whether you can match the service request, the object identification and the inspection records item by item, and explain clearly when the records conflict. Tire service requires hands-on work and cooperation; the paper experience only offers clues about checking habits, and the actual physical demands, operating training and customer communication still need to be learned separately.
The experience on this page is not a repair qualification, a vehicle safety inspection or a hiring test, and passing the paper exercise cannot be used to claim you can operate equipment.

Specific signals include confirming the work order number and vehicle identification before checking the requirements and records; being able to separate the customer's description, the technician's inspection results and your own guesses; and keeping both versions after a revision. Being willing to stay accurate when checking the same kind of information repeatedly, and being able to state clearly which basis is missing when uncertain, is more informative than finding one obvious error once.

Signals that call for caution include treating blank fields as already checked, writing in unobserved results to meet a vehicle delivery deadline, substituting on the basis of a similar model on your own, or equating being able to read records with being able to repair independently. Concerns about noise, standing, roadside work and shifts need to be discussed together with the actual controls and arrangements; do not use personality type to rule someone out, and do not rely on an interest label to promise that you can adapt.

After finishing the experience, keep the initial questions, the revised conclusions and the matters still awaiting confirmation. Observe whether you are willing to check once more, and choose a real role to learn about training and how the service work is divided; do not treat a record review result as a conclusion about the vehicle's condition.

The United States counterpart is O*NET-SOC49-3093.00 Tire Repairers and Changers, defined as repairing and replacing tires. The task list includes wheel mounting and dismounting, balancing, repair, inspection and some retreading work; it is understood separately from the occupational files for whole-vehicle repair and for machine tire manufacturing.

Inputs may include the service request, vehicle and tire identification, inspection records and parts information. First establish which object is being handled this time and the scope already confirmed; symptoms described by the customer and professional inspection results cannot be equated directly.

Identifying tire size, construction and related markings is part of the task, while matching and safety judgements still rest on manufacturer material, on-site equipment and professional processes. This page does not provide pressure, torque, load or size substitution rules.

Shop tasks may involve tire replacement, repair and balancing. The task order and the permitted scope are set by the actual equipment, vehicle and training; the process below only helps you understand the relationship between service and records, and is not a repair operating tutorial.

When the service object or the inspection results change, re-check the work order and the materials. Any defect, missing item or inconsistency found should be recorded and handed to the responsible person for confirmation; a single photograph or this page's practice cannot be used to judge whether a real tire can be repaired or used.

Communicate the service request and anomalies with the vehicle intake staff, colleagues and the supervising technician; some tasks also involve explaining to customers and roadside service. Who may decide the repair plan, replacement parts or delivery must be confirmed according to the actual division of duties.

The O*NET work context involves standing, repetitive hand operations, noise, contaminants, bending the body and outdoor weather, among others. The material describes the requirements of an occupational group, not an accident rate or an individual health diagnosis.

Handover retains the object, the inspection and processing records already completed and the questions awaiting confirmation. A completed work order does not automatically prove that the repair is finished or the vehicle is safe; professional inspection and delivery authority are confirmed separately.

The following organises shop service and roadside service into task understanding lines. The two are not service models that every employer follows, and actual tasks follow the specific role, vehicle, tools and training.
Shop tire service
Receive the request → check the object and scope → professional inspection → confirm the handling arrangement → handle and record → professional re-check and handover
The tire handling result within the confirmed scope, the inspection records and the service handover information
Roadside tire service
Check the request and the location → confirm the service conditions → assess on arrival → handle within the trained scope → record anomalies → hand over to the responsible person
The service result within the scope confirmed on site, plus records of the location, object, conditions and open items
Shared work foundation
Object identification · professional inspection · trained operation · service communication · anomaly records · handover checking
Shop service and roadside service: how do the objects, cooperation and boundaries differ?

Shop service takes place at a fixed work location; roadside service also requires understanding the requested location and the on-site conditions. The shared task is tire service and records, but the environment, tools and cooperation may change. This is an editorial comparison based on the O*NET tasks and does not presume that the same repair can be done at any location.
Core purpose
Complete the agreed tire service under the conditions confirmed in the shop, keeping inspection, handling and handover consistent.
Handle the tire need within the on-site confirmed conditions and service scope, keeping the on-site limits and open items.
Main objects and basis
The service request, vehicle and tire information, professional inspection and shop rules.
The service request, object information, location and on-site assessment, plus the available tools and trained scope.
Core process
Vehicle intake communication, professional inspection, handling according to the confirmed arrangement, re-checking and recording.
Check the location conditions, carry out an on-site professional assessment, handle within the confirmed scope and hand over to the responsible person.
Main outputs
The service result within the agreed scope, and work orders that can be matched to the vehicle, tires and handling.
The on-site service result, a statement of conditions and a record of the items that could not be completed on the spot.
Responsible party
The operator carries out trained tasks; the repair plan, anomaly handling and delivery are confirmed according to the shop's division of duties.
Service staff work within clearly defined tasks and safety conditions; anything beyond those conditions is handed to the responsible person.
How they cooperate
Communicate requirements with intake staff, technicians, parts staff and customers, avoiding any mismatch between what is said and the work order.
Check the location, object and on-site limits with the requester and the responsible person, and confirm again when they change.
Delivery boundaries
Complete records do not mean the vehicle is in acceptable condition; do not make mounting, inflation or repair judgements on your own on the basis of this page.
Arriving on site does not mean the service conditions exist; this page does not provide roadside work or vehicle lifting steps.
Key occupational judgements

These questions are used to understand service records and the chain of responsibility; they are an editorial self-check. Real repair and safety decisions are carried out by trained staff under the specific process and cannot be replaced by paper answers.
Can the object of this service be matched one to one with the work order?
Are the customer's description and the professional inspection results recorded separately?
After the object or the on-site conditions change, which confirmations need to be made again?
When identification conflicts or missing inspection items appear, how should you raise the question?

Write down the work order, the conflicting fields, both original values and the handover conditions affected; keep the original records and ask the responsible person to verify. Do not choose a value that looks reasonable on your own just to complete the records.
Is the task within your own training, tools and authorisation?

State what you have not been trained for or confirmed, and leave it to the responsible person to arrange. Not knowing how to perform an operation should not be made up for by imitating public videos; this page contains no steps for wheel mounting and dismounting, lifting, inflation or rim work.
At handover, can you distinguish confirmed, pending and not-performed items?
Vehicle intake｜service request and object check｜Listen to the requirement, check the wheel and tire identification and record the information awaiting confirmation.
Mounting and dismounting｜wheel and tire replacement｜Carry out tire service according to the specific vehicle, equipment and training, and do not let paper practice stand in for operating preparation.
Balancing｜testing and counterweight tasks｜O*NET lists balancing machines and counterweight tasks; this page does not specify equipment settings or counterweight operating methods.
Repair｜tire condition and handling｜Tasks such as checking defects and carrying out repairs follow a professional process, and this page is not used to judge whether damage can be repaired.
Re-checking｜results and anomaly records｜Record the inspection and handling against the service scope, and hand anomalies to the responsible person for confirmation.
Roadside｜on-site service and handover｜Check the location conditions and the trained scope, and leave a record of the service result and the items that could not be completed.
Section title｜The working environment and working style of tire repairers and changers

The tasks largely involve hands-on work and cooperation with people. Shop and roadside conditions differ, and standing, moving loads, noise and weather are worth learning about in advance; the actual intensity, rest and control measures need to be checked specifically.

Organisation and location｜The tasks may be carried out at a repair service location or at the requested location. O*NET lists service vehicle on-site handling tasks, but that does not prove that all workers go out on the road; the Jiaozuo material supports only the recruitment information of one historical tire repair shop.

Materials and tools｜Tires, rims, valve stems, tools and balancing equipment relate to the specific task. The O*NET software list includes record systems, databases, email, estimating and office software; it does not show that every shop uses the same product, and it certainly does not mean AI has been adopted.

The service request, vehicle condition and inspection results affect the arrangement. The task list is not a universal operating sequence, and the safe use of each piece of equipment and the professional re-check follow the actual training and rules.

Pace and intensity｜The occupational context involves standing, bending or kneeling, hand activity and load-related requirements; shop scheduling and roadside arrangements need to be checked with the actual employer. This page has no evidence of a national shift pattern or a daily vehicle intake volume.

When communicating, give the object, the observation and the original record, rather than only saying "this tire is bad". Customer requirements, professional judgements and completed service are stated separately, and anything beyond the confirmed scope goes first to the responsible person.

Re-checking and the chain of responsibility｜Vehicle intake, professional inspection, operation and delivery may be handled by different people. Recording an anomaly helps handover, but it does not mean you hold authority to change the plan, release the vehicle or operate the business.

Quality observation｜Understanding the job can be judged by whether the objects match, whether records are truthful, whether the service scope is confirmed and whether anomalies can be passed on. These are ways of understanding the tasks, not a vehicle safety inspection standard or a uniform employer assessment.
Professional basis and boundaries of use
The tire mounting and dismounting, balancing, repair, roadside service and context material of the precise United States occupation
The employment, wages and typical education, experience and training categories of the separately listed United States occupation
Jiaozuo 2024 historical recruitment by a tire repair shop; limited to what the original posting disclosed
The official Jiangsu catalogue includes the 2018 standard for the automobile repair worker; a broad trade is not automatically equivalent to this occupation
United States rules for servicing large vehicle rims; there is an explicit exclusion for automobile or light truck tires used on cars, pickups and vans

Tire repairers and changers repair or replace vehicle tires, with tasks involving wheel mounting and dismounting, balancing, tire repair, inspection and service records, and they may also provide roadside service. The United States O*NET49-3093.00 list also includes some retreading work; it is understood separately from the independent occupations of machine tire building, whole-vehicle repair and diesel engine repair, and specific operations and release follow the actual training and division of duties.

Diagnosing, adjusting, repairing or overhauling automobiles, with outputs covering the vehicle's related systems; tire service experience does not automatically prove whole-vehicle diagnostic ability.
Repairing buses, trucks and diesel engines, involving broader mechanical tasks such as braking and steering; large vehicle tire service cannot be equated with diesel engine repair.
Repairing, adjusting and assembling bicycles, involving gearing, braking and wheelsets as well as tires and inner tubes; the objects differ from motor vehicle tire service.

Operating equipment to manufacture tires, including retreading tasks; this is a different occupational basis from shop tire replacement, and similar handling tasks in part do not mean the two are fully interchangeable.

Check the on-site conditions at the requested location, handle within the confirmed scope and record the items that cannot be completed.

Being willing to check the location, task and tools in advance, and to speak up promptly when conditions change.
Automotive service technicians and mechanics
Whole-vehicle system diagnosis and repair ability needs to be filled in, verified by evidence of work on the corresponding system.
More interested in whole-vehicle faults, and willing to check the training and job conditions separately.
Bus and truck mechanics and diesel engine specialists
An understanding of heavy vehicle and diesel engine mechanical systems is needed, and tire handling experience can only provide part of the foundation.
Wanting to deal with a broader range of vehicle and engine problems, and willing to take the target role's training.
Bicycle repairers
With the object changed to bicycles, gearing, braking, assembly and adjustment tasks need to be filled in; automobile operations cannot simply be copied.
Being willing to work on several bicycle systems, and to show repair preparation for the corresponding object.
Tire builders
The object centres on building tires or carrying out retreading operations with materials and equipment, and the factory pace, training and responsibility are checked separately.
More interested in material assembly and production records, and willing to check the specific manufacturing tasks first.
How should shop service, roadside service and the adjacent repair and manufacturing occupations be chosen between?

First choose the task you are willing to keep doing: fixed shop service and roadside handling are understanding directions inside this occupation, while whole-vehicle repair, diesel engines, bicycles and tire manufacturing have their own objects and outputs. Taking part in the same service chain does not mean the duties are the same, and liking a particular kind of vehicle cannot replace the corresponding training and checking of the environment.

You can start with the vehicle intake record experience to observe object checking and explaining anomalies, then learn about training and the division of duties from a specific role. If you want to move into whole-vehicle work, diesel engines, bicycles or manufacturing, prepare task evidence for the target object; do not treat one record exercise or your existing service experience as a qualification for the target occupation.

The comparison uses the separate O*NET files for this occupation and the four targets. The internal directions and suitability signals are an editorial summary, and the adjacent occupations' wages, training and authority are not merged; actual job requirements in China are still checked against the current employer and the applicable rules.
Once the actual task is chosen, look at whether a tool changes vehicle intake records, identification or professional operations, and check the evidence and responsibility for each separately.

At the ability level, a text tool can help organise the fictional vehicle intake material into a field list, or turn a vague question into one that can be answered. This is an editorial suggestion; the output still needs to be checked line by line against the original material, and the tool must not be allowed to fabricate vehicle identification, inspection results or repair parameters.

Licence plate recognition and tire judgement are different tasks. The Hunter and SKAIVISION announcement describes licence plate recognition at the service lane, matching customer records and process timing; it does not verify tire defect diagnosis, repairability or vehicle safety.

Insufficient evidence: the national AI usage rate, net task time saved and income effects for tire repairers and changers. One vendor integration announcement does not show that all shops have adopted it, nor does it prove that a particular repair task has been taken over by AI.

Control starts with the task scope: let the tool handle only the explicitly permitted record organisation, and check the material source, field definitions and receiving permission. For real customer data, confirm the tool and its purpose under the shop's rules, and do not upload it just because it is convenient.

O*NET lists object identification, tire inspection, balancing, repair and on-site service tasks; it does not prove that a licence plate recognition tool has completed a professional inspection or repair.

Recognition or record results cannot replace a professional inspection. O*NET lists tire condition inspection, repair and balancing as separate tasks; the actual object, the inspection and the trained operation each need to be confirmed. The occupational task list is not an operating procedure, and this page provides no repair parameters.

The remaining responsibilities include confirming the object, carrying out the professional inspection, checking the repair plan and completing a safe handover. A record organisation tool does not thereby gain operating or release authority, and its output should be checked by the person actually responsible.

Insufficient evidence: causal research showing that AI alone has caused a net employment change in the tire service occupation. The BLS2025—2035 growth of 3.4% is an overall occupational projection, and the number of jobs added or lost because of AI, or an individual's probability of unemployment, cannot be separated out of it.

The general framework supports defining the record task and checking the input and output first, then arranging risk management. On that basis this page proposes an editorial method for checking vehicle intake fields, without claiming that the method has been verified for time saved, accuracy or occupational employment effects.
Which tasks and responsibilities in tire service will AI change?

Insufficient evidence: reviewable task scores, national AI adoption and net employment causal results for this occupation. The case checked is limited to licence plate and customer record matching, and repair safety still requires professional confirmation; the BLS2025—2035 overall growth of 3.4%, the ten-year net increase of about 3800 people and the average annual 12900 openings that includes replacements are component indicators and do not represent an AI effect. AI Impact Score 17% is an editorial estimate. There are also the Hunter licence plate integration and the United States rim scope cases, whose original text appears in the sources and the relevant sections; neither is treated as evidence of tire diagnosis or of effects across the whole occupation.

Can a text tool replace the vehicle intake check?

It can organise a draft, but the object, requirements and inspection status still need to be confirmed against the original records. You can use S1 on this page to compare whether the tool preserves missing items and conflicts; producing a tidy table is not the same as the fields being true, nor does it prove that the service has been completed.
Can licence plate or text recognition replace a tire inspection?

Recognition capability cannot be used to infer that a professional inspection has been completed. O*NET lists tire inspection, balancing and repair as specific tasks; recording the object and judging the real condition of a tire are different questions, and the actual professional process is checked separately.
Does a system match result mean you can start working?

The object, service scope, equipment conditions and trained personnel still need to be confirmed under the actual process. A result returned by the system is not the same as the customer agreement, a professional inspection or authorisation being in place, and unknown conditions cannot be passed by default.
Can recognition and record results replace a professional inspection?
How many tire service jobs will AI reduce?

Insufficient evidence: a net employment change figure for this occupation that can be attributed to AI. The overall BLS projection includes many factors, and a vendor's description of a process tool is not employment research; no individual probability of unemployment or hiring is calculated.
Can typical United States training be applied directly to Chinese shops?

It cannot be applied automatically. The BLS category of a high school diploma or equivalent, no related experience and short-term on-the-job training is a United States statistical category, not a uniform entry, training or assessment requirement for all jobs in China. The actual employer and local conditions are checked separately.

Insufficient evidence: the national wage median and percentiles for tire repairers and changers in mainland China. The pre-tax annual average of 79,857 yuan for social production and life service personnel in enterprises above the designated size in 2025 covers many categories of personnel including repair and fabrication services; it is used as a broad reference for tire service tasks, not as a separately listed wage, starting pay or personal range for tire workers.

When comparing specific roles, check the pay cycle, base wage, service commission or piece rate, overtime, probation period, allowances and payment arrangements. An amount in the original posting with no cycle cannot be written as a monthly wage on your own, and an unknown pay structure should be asked about item by item.

For resident services, repair and other services, the 2025 urban non-private figure is 70,226 yuan per year and the private figure is 52,059 yuan per year; both are pre-tax broad industry annual averages and cover a different population from the 79,857 yuan for broad service roles in enterprises above the designated size. They are not personal upper and lower limits, and they exclude self-employed businesses and freelancers.

Item 204 in the Jiaozuo public employment website 2024-02-08 spring action summary: a Bridgestone tire repair shop recruited 2 repair workers with pay of 2000—3000 yuan, requiring the ability to repair. The pay cycle and the specific tire tasks are not specified, so it serves only as a historical single-shop related sample and is not treated as currently open.

The historical posting does not list pre-tax or post-tax treatment, base wage or overtime structure, and the age column also contains a text error, so no age threshold is set from it. The amount, requirements and number of places explain only this one item of information and cannot be used to infer that a vacancy still exists.
China wages: the precise occupational gap, the broad industry background and the historical single-shop quote
The historical quote is 2000—3000 yuan, and the original posting does not state a cycle; it cannot be written up as a monthly or annual wage.

Insufficient evidence: the pay cycle and pay structure of the historical single shop, and a current comparable national occupational sample, were not obtained. Other tire workers with the same name or whole-vehicle repair quotes are not mixed in.

The original posting supports only the disclosed conditions such as being able to repair; the specific tasks, training and assessment are not stated, and it cannot be expanded into hiring criteria for all shops.
The 2 places in the same posting are not 2 independent employer samples. From one historical repair shop alone, differences in current regional wages or national demand cannot be compared.

The National Bureau of Statistics average for the broad repair related industry provides background; the two ownership values cannot be used to place an individual tire worker in a bracket, nor can they guarantee that all related shops fall into that industry.

Insufficient evidence: currently representative Chinese tire service recruitment and comparable wage data. Public employment, government recruitment and industry statistics were checked; mixed trades at a manufacturing plant or tire workers with unidentified tasks are not used to pad the sample.

Check the actual shop's paid hours, shift rotation, roadside service and probation arrangements, and compare commuting with known costs. A historical quote does not prove that the work continues, nor does it promise allowance or service commission rules.

Insufficient evidence: occupational evidence that AI adoption has changed Chinese tire service wages. Licence plate record integration does not measure individual pay, and the record organisation suggestion cannot be converted into a pay cut figure either; pay is still checked against the actual tasks and pay structure.

The 2025 broad service role figure of 79,857 yuan and the repair related industry figures of 70,226 yuan for non-private and 52,059 yuan for private are all pre-tax annual averages covering different populations, and are not a separately listed distribution for tire workers. The Jiaozuo 2024 historical single shop figure of 2000—3000 yuan does not state a cycle and is not supplemented with a monthly wage; United States wages are not converted to fill the China gap, and self-employment receipts are kept separate from employee wages.

The 2025 national wage median for United States tire repairers and changers is 37710 US dollars per year and 18.13 US dollars per hour. The original table gives both the annual and the hourly value; they are not an individual's take-home income, starting pay or actual paid arrangement for the whole year.
The 2025 10th percentile is 30010 US dollars per year and 14.43 US dollars per hour, the lower part of the national wage distribution, not a guaranteed rate for someone with no experience.

The 2025 90th percentile is 50230 US dollars per year and 24.15 US dollars per hour, the higher part of the wage distribution, and does not correspond to a uniform senior worker grade or a sustained high income for an individual every year.

The BLS2025—2035 projection is growth of 3.4%; employment is 112200 in 2025 and about 116000 in 2035, a ten-year net increase of about 3800 people. The average of about 12900 openings a year includes replacement demand and differs from the net increase and from the current number of job openings.

OEWS wages exclude the self-employed; the employment projection has its own coverage. The EP table lists a self-employment share of 2.4% of employment in 2025, which does not mean that wage percentiles include their business income, and the two kinds of statistics cannot be used to estimate an individual's self-employment income.

This page adopts the official annual and hourly values from the same table directly and does not calculate an individual annual salary from fixed hours. The actual shifts, overtime, service commission and paid time are checked against the specific role, and a statistical value does not guarantee an individual's working hours.

The 2025 national wage distribution for United States tire service occupations
The median sits in the middle of the national wage distribution; it is not an entry rate, a take-home amount or a seniority threshold. Both wage units come from the same official table.
How can national percentiles be used to compare roles?

Percentiles describe a statistical position rather than years of service or a grade, and P25 and P75 are also adopted directly from the original table. values: S1｜fictional vehicle intake records

All the material is an original paper prompt. Vehicle intake card T08: object B7, the request is tire service, status "awaiting professional inspection". Inspection sheet T08: object B9, the inspection result and the responsible person's sign-off are blank. Parts record T08: object B7, handling status "use not yet confirmed".

Practice rule: only when the three records for the same work order have consistent objects, both the inspection result and the responsible person's confirmation have clear records, and the parts use status is confirmed, may you write "the material can move to the next round of handover confirmation". Any conflict or unknown should be written as awaiting confirmation, and no judgement about vehicle safety is made.
Your task and the S2 revision

In the first round, write the object conflict, the unknown fields and two clarifying questions. S2 makes clear that the responsible person corrects the inspection sheet object B9 to B7, on the basis of the object confirmation record newly added to the prompt; the inspection result, sign-off and parts status are unchanged.

In the second round, update the object conclusion and list the remaining items awaiting confirmation; hand in one initial checking table, the revision table, the question list and the boundary statement, without operating any vehicle or equipment.
Complete reference answer

S1: the work order numbers are all T08; the object B7/B9 conflicts; the inspection result and sign-off are blank, and the parts are unconfirmed. Question one asks the responsible person to check the object and provide the basis for the correction, and question two asks whether the professional inspection and sign-off are complete and what the parts status is. It cannot move to handover confirmation.

S2: all three objects are B7 and the conflict is resolved; the inspection result, sign-off and parts status are still unknown. It therefore still awaits confirmation and cannot be written as fully passed. Only records that later clearly complete these conditions can support a material conclusion under the prompt, and that still does not mean the vehicle is safe.
Experience boundaries

Only read the fictional material, write questions and record revisions; do not mount or dismount, lift, inflate, repair or test drive. The object B7/B9 is a fictional identifier, not a vehicle model or tire parameter. The practice provides no repair plan, pressure, torque or safety judgement, and requires no upload of customer data or purchase of tools.

Recent graduates and career changers: understand the task first, then check the training entry point

The stages are for organising evidence of ability, not a uniform grade or a fixed promotion period. The actual operating scope, feedback and employer conditions need to be confirmed each time, and you cannot assume from years of service that you can handle every vehicle.
China and the United States apply separately

The Chinese material is one 2024 Jiaozuo historical single-shop related recruitment; the United States uses the typical education, experience and training categories for 49-3093. Current roles and local conditions are checked separately, and the two are not automatically mutually recognised.

United States typical training, the Chinese broad trade standard and shop equipment training are checked separately. Insufficient evidence: China's current precise entry requirements and local registration conditions; neither the catalogue nor a paper piece can prove that all jobs are licensed.
Understanding tasks and records
Separate the service request, the object and the inspection status, list the missing items clearly, and honestly state what you have not yet been trained for.
Receiving specific training and feedback
Learn tire tasks and equipment within the actual arrangements, with feedback tied to specific operations; this page only practises paper checking.
Staying accurate and handing over
Across several tasks, keep the objects consistent, the records truthful and the anomalies explained, and do not treat familiarity as a reason to skip confirmation.
Checking complex tasks and expansion
When the vehicle, equipment or service location changes, re-check the training and the responsible person, and verify the target adjacent duties separately.
Understanding shop service and the trained path
Task exploration
First learn about the shop's vehicle types, service requests and division of duties, and complete the S1 paper check.
Being able to point out the object conflict and the unknown checks, and state that you carried out no operations.
Training and job conditions are checked with the actual employer; a paper experience is not a qualification.
Choose one specific service task to learn about the training and equipment.
Trained participation
Learn the specified tasks within the actual training and supervision arrangements, and state the parts you have not yet mastered.
Genuine trained feedback and a record of the scope, without using S1 to claim operation.
Equipment, vehicles and authority are confirmed by role; do not expand the scope on your own.
Fill in one specific gap and ask about how inspection and handover are divided.
Accuracy across repeated tasks
Within the confirmed scope, keep the object, service records and professional re-check consistent.
Repeated real feedback can show how anomalies are handed over, and the records are not fabricated.
Proficiency is not plan-change or vehicle release authority.
Check whether new equipment or new vehicle tasks need to be learned.
Expanding the service scope
After a task change, confirm the training, tools and responsibility again, and do not assume competence from years of service.
Genuine training and feedback on the new task, making clear what is still unknown.
Broader whole-vehicle repair is a change of target duty, and qualifications and training are checked separately.
Continue with the tire main line or choose one target occupation to fill in the corresponding ability.
Roadside service conditions and the cooperation path
Check the on-site task
Learn about the roadside location, object, tools and responsible person, and produce a paper question list first.
Being able to list what to ask when the location and conditions are unknown, without providing road operations.
Whether the actual role goes out on the road needs checking; it is not a uniform requirement for all workers.
Learn whether the real attendance and training arrangements suit your living conditions.
Trained on-site participation
Check the service scope under the actual arrangements, and explain to the responsible person when conditions change.
Genuine training and on-site feedback records, clearly showing the part you took on.
Safety procedures, vehicles and on-site conditions cannot be replaced by a text tool.
Fill in the ability to communicate on site and state the limits clearly.
Handover across requests
Across different locations and requests, still keep the object, the limits and the open items.
Being able to explain how a change of conditions was re-confirmed and handed over once.
Arriving on site does not mean you have authority to handle every problem.
Check the training needed for the new location, equipment and task.
Judging complex requests
When a task goes beyond the tools, training or conditions, confirm the arrangement along the chain of responsibility.
Real feedback can show that the limits were stated accurately, without presenting the unknown as complete.
This page provides no road set-up, lifting or inflation procedures.
Check whether to continue with the roadside main line or the fixed shop direction, comparing the conditions for each.
Deepening records and service communication
Reading the records
Separate the customer's description, the inspection and the handling status, and keep the unknowns.
The S1 initial original-value table and two clarifying questions.
An editorial paper entry point, not a uniform employer examination.
Check how an actual shop uses the records.
Checking the basis for the revision
After the object is corrected, update only the fields affected and re-check the remaining conditions.
The S2 version comparison still keeps the inspection and parts as awaiting confirmation.
A generated table does not prove that the original values are true or that the professional inspection is complete.
Learn who is responsible for real records and how feedback flows.
Stable service communication
Accurately restate the requirement, status and limits within the tasks actually permitted.
Specific real feedback and your own contribution, without inventing customer experience.
Polite communication cannot replace the professional plan and authorisation.
Fill in clarifying vague requests and handing over information.
Expanding process cooperation
Broader record or coordination duties require the data permission and work scope to be checked first.
You can show your own permitted process, with anonymity and public disclosure checked separately.
